title: Formulation of a protocol to evaluate the aerobic granulation potential (AGP) of an inoculum
author: Penagos, Victoria, et al.
materials: In contrast to other widely used substrates such as glucose, different studies have emphasized acetate as an efficient carbon source for growing granules. Acetate promotes the production of extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) [61], and granule-forming microorganisms (Methanosarcina and Methanothrix) prefer it [39]. The granules derived from acetate appeared to be more compact and had better sedimentation characteristics [63]. Furthermore, acetate is considered a biodegradable substrate that is rapidly assimilated by granule-forming microorganisms [46], thus making it an option to determine the effect of the inoculum without the intervention of the substrate composition.

The application of the protocol begins with the start-up of a sequential batch reactor (SBR) used as the experimental unit. This reactor type has been widely used and is highly recommended for aerobic granulation because a discontinuous operation is advantageous to the process. Furthermore, the SBR creates an adverse environment and stress conditions for the microbiota that lead to aggregation as a survival mechanism [63], promoting the selection of granular biomass and the wash-out of flocculent or filamentous microorganisms [26].

steps.title: Prepare mineral and micronutrient stocks
steps.instruction: Make two stock solutions: (a) mineral salts – dipotassium phosphate (K₂HPO₄) 63.75 g L⁻¹ (add 3.75 mL L⁻¹), dipotassium phosphate (K₂HPO₄) 61.04 g L⁻¹ (add 1.04 mL L⁻¹), sodium chloride (NaCl) 122 g L⁻¹ (add 0.80 mL L⁻¹), magnesium chloride hexahydrate (MgCl₂·6H₂O) 23.5 g L⁻¹; (b) micronutrients – ferric chloride hexahydrate (FeCl₃·6H₂O) 1.35 g L⁻¹, magnesium chloride tetrahydrate (MgCl₂·4H₂O) 0.10 g L⁻¹, cobalt chloride hexahydrate (CoCl₂·6H₂O) 0.02 g L⁻¹, calcium chloride dihydrate (CaCl₂·2H₂O) 0.10 g L⁻¹, zinc chloride (ZnCl₂) 0.10 g L⁻¹, copper chloride dihydrate (CuCl₂·2H₂O) 0.02 g L⁻¹, trioxoboric acid (H₃BO₃) 0.01 g L⁻¹, sodium chloride (NaCl) 1.00 g L⁻¹, sodium selenite pentahydrate (Na₂SeO₃·5H₂O) 0.03 g L⁻¹, nickel chloride hexahydrate (NiCl₂·6H₂O) 0.12 g L⁻¹. Store stocks refrigerated.

steps.title: Prepare acetate substrate solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve sodium acetate (Na₃CH₃COO) in de‑ionised water and add the mineral‑salt and micronutrient stocks to obtain a substrate COD of 1500 mg L⁻¹ (corresponding to an organic loading rate of 6.00 kg m⁻³ d⁻¹). Adjust the final volume according to the desired OLR.

steps.title: Adapt inoculum to acetate
steps.instruction: Mix the activated‑sludge inoculum with the acetate substrate in a 1 : 1 (vol/vol) ratio inside an aerated conical vessel. Keep the mixture aerated and monitor COD reduction; continue until COD has decreased by more than 40 % of the initial value.

steps.title: Select and homogenise adapted inoculum
steps.instruction: Fill a 1 L Imhoff cone with the adapted sludge, stir gently, let settle for 2 min, then discard the supernatant. Repeat the fill‑settle‑decant cycle until the total required inoculum volume is obtained. Homogenise the collected sludge and determine total suspended solids (TSS) and volatile suspended solids (VSS) according to Standard Methods.

steps.title: Set up the SBR reactor
steps.instruction: Install the fiberglass sequential‑batch reactor (working volume 280 L, internal diameter 0.02 m, effective height 0.98 m). Connect the bottom diffuser to an air pump, place influent and effluent ports at mid‑height, and set the volumetric exchange ratio to 50 %. Adjust the up‑flow shear force by varying the airflow rate (2.40–3.00 cm s⁻¹). Verify temperature control (20–25 °C) and pH probe, DO probe, and Arduino‑controlled cycle timing.

steps.title: Inoculate reactor to target F/M
steps.instruction: Add the selected inoculum to the reactor to achieve an F/M ratio of 0.64 g DQO (g SS V)⁻¹. In the first cycle, add an extra 50 mL of inoculum to the seeding volume for accurate solids measurement.

steps.title: Run SBR cycles – Phase 1 (days 1‑8)
steps.instruction: Operate cycles of 3 h total time with the following stage durations: feeding 1 min, aeration 63 min, settling 15 min, discharge 18 min. Maintain pH 6.5–8.0, DO 0.5–6.0 mg L⁻¹, temperature 20–25 °C, and aeration rate 2.40–3.00 cm s⁻¹. Record COD of influent, effluent and mixed liquor each cycle.

steps.title: Run SBR cycles – Phase 2 (day 9)
steps.instruction: Change stage times to: feeding 2 min, aeration 73 min, settling 5 min, discharge 11 min. Keep all other operational parameters unchanged and continue monitoring the same analytical variables.

steps.title: Run SBR cycles – Phase 3 (days 10‑11)
steps.instruction: Change stage times to: feeding 1 min, aeration 76 min, settling 2 min, discharge 12 min. Continue analytical monitoring.

steps.title: Sample for microscopy and morphology
steps.instruction: During each aeration stage, withdraw 50 mL of mixed liquor from the reactor bottom. Place the sample on a Neubauer chamber, capture images with a microscope equipped with a camera at 4×, 10×, 40× and 100× magnifications using identical settings. Process the images in graphic‑design software, using the Neubauer grid as a scale, and measure equivalent diameter (Deq), circularity and roundness.

substeps.instruction: Calculate Deq = 2 × √(Area / π) where Area is obtained from the software (µm²).

steps.title: Determine settling velocity of granules
steps.instruction: Select spherical aerobic granules (>0.20 mm). Fill a 1 L graduated cylinder with tap water, gently pour the granules onto the water surface, start a stopwatch immediately, and record the time (t) required for the granules to reach the bottom. Compute Vs = L / t (m s⁻¹) where L is the travel distance (m). A positive result is Vs ≥ 10 m s⁻¹ (or ≥ 8 m h⁻¹ as reported).

steps.title: Measure sludge volumetric index (SVI)
steps.instruction: Follow Standard Methods (APHA et al., 2005) to determine SVI of the mixed liquor at the end of each phase. Compare values with the SVI scale (e.g., SVI ≈ 150 mL g⁻¹ indicates poor settling).

steps.title: Continue operation until granulation
steps.instruction: Run the SBR for up to ~11 days, or stop earlier if granulation criteria are met: granule diameter > 0.20 mm, settling velocity ≥ 10 m s⁻¹, circularity ≥ 0.70, roundness ≥ 0.70, and SVI in the low range (< 50 mL g⁻¹).

steps.title: Terminate run and collect final samples
steps.instruction: Empty the entire reactor content into a container, homogenise the sludge, and take samples for final SVI, settling‑velocity, and morphological analyses (photography, image processing). Record all data with the same camera settings used throughout the experiment.

steps.title: Data analysis and literature comparison
steps.instruction: Compile COD removal, pH, DO, temperature, SVI, settling velocity, equivalent diameter, circularity and roundness data. Compare the results with the published criteria (e.g., COD removal > 85 % after ~25 cycles, settling velocity ≥ 8 m h⁻¹, circularity/roundness ≈ 0.70) to confirm successful aerobic granulation.
